An atom index you give to any tool other than crossover_molecules is always interpreted against your current working molecule, never against ligand 2 - do not reason about 'modifying ligand 2' and then call one of these tools, since the edit will land on the wrong molecule and likely do nothing you intended.

Goal: I want to maximize jnk3, qed scores; minimize sa score. Please propose a new molecule better than the current molecule. I have given you two candidate ligands. You are encouraged to make a crossover between the candidate molecules on the first step, then mutate the resulting molecule. Only make a few modifications (at most 3), then respond with FINAL ANSWER. Do not let molecular weight exceed 700.

Ligand 1 is the azetidine-piperazinium host again, and ligand 2 is a rigid fused chromone-lactam (SA 2.73, 1 rotatable bond) with no activity - a crossover would mostly import that strained tricycle at random, so I will do a directed rebuild instead. Having already put an indazole on this exact scaffold at this exact anchor, repeating the operation with a different core gives a matched-scaffold comparison of chemotypes. Cut non-ring bond 11-12 to drop the protonated piperazine (which is what holds QED at 0.63 and LogP at -1.70) and graft carbazol-3-yl: a planar tricyclic aromatic with an NH donor, which is the cheapest structural mimic available of the anthrapyrazolone core of the reference JNK inhibitor SP600125, and also the core of the carbazole-carboxamide JNK series. It is a much larger, flatter, more distinctive graft than the indazole, so it tests both chemotype and planarity on a scaffold I already have a baseline for.

Good: QED 0.634 -> 0.721, SA 3.80 -> 2.51, charge gone, three aromatic rings where there were none. Now the same cleanup as before - the isopropoxyethyl tail on the sulfonyl (atoms 0-5) is 4 of the 6 rotatable bonds and ~100 Da of ballast. Cut the non-ring S-CH2 bond 6-5 and put a methyl there to give the methanesulfonyl azetidine at ~300 Da. This also makes the molecule structurally matched to the indazole version I built on this same scaffold, so the only difference between the two offspring is the fused core itself.
